source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: ARCH Disability Law Centre
entries.description: A specialty legal clinic that practises only disability rights law in Ontario. Its free, confidential Summary Advice and Referral Service, a province-wide telephone service, gives people with disabilities legal advice on areas such as human rights, accessibility, education, transportation and decision-making rights.
entries.cost_note: The Summary Advice and Referral Service is free; for further legal services, Legal Aid Ontario's financial eligibility criteria apply.
entries.evidence: a free, confidential legal service directly to persons with disabilities from across Ontario on certain disability-related areas of law
entries.notes: CNAF lists it on its national page; it serves Ontario only. The phone service is closed 1-2 pm daily and all day Mondays (contact page); parents, guardians and support persons may take part with the person's consent. Office at 55 University Ave, 15th Floor, Toronto.

entries.name: ODSP Action Coalition
entries.description: A provincial, volunteer grassroots group led by people with disabilities on the Ontario Disability Support Program (ODSP) that advocates for better income and other supports. It holds community events and meetings and welcomes members, but does not give legal advice or help with individual ODSP cases.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: ODSP Action Coalition is a provincial, volunteer grassroots advocacy group led by people with disabilities on ODSP, with a network of valued allies, that advocates for improvements to the income and other supports available to people with disabilities.
entries.notes: CNAF lists it on its national page; it serves Ontario only. Contact is by an email written out on the site in words (a gmail account), so no email is given. Latest posts are from September 2026. ODSP itself is already in scripts/data/services/funding.json as ontario-disability-support-program.

entries.name: Individualized Funding Coalition for Ontario (IFCO)
entries.description: A coalition of people with disabilities, their families, trusted others and allies that works to move individualized funding forward in Ontario, so that funding and independent facilitation help people build a meaningful life in their community. It shares papers, presentations and a podcast, holds events, and welcomes members.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: We are a coalition of people with disabilities, their families and trusted others as well as allies working together to ensure that individualized funding approaches in Ontario, support people to create a meaningful life in their community.
entries.notes: CNAF lists it on its national page; it serves Ontario only. The latest dated item on the home page is November 2024 (a podcast episode). The email is the coalition's general gmail address; the phone number on the site is a named person's voicemail extension and the mailing address is care of an office in Windsor, so neither is given.

entries.name: Ontario Bursary for Students with Disabilities (BSWD)
entries.description: Ontario's bursary helps eligible full-time and part-time postsecondary students pay for disability-related educational services and equipment, such as note-takers, tutors and assistive technology, up to $2,000 a year. The same application covers the federal Canada Student Grant for Services and Equipment (up to $20,000), and students at public schools complete it with their school's accessibility office.
entries.cost_note: Government bursary; the page does not mention any fee to apply.
entries.evidence: help eligible full-time and part-time students pay for eligible disability-related services and equipment needed to participate in postsecondary studies
entries.notes: CNAF lists it on its national page; the bursary is for Ontario (OSAP) students. Students must have a verified disability and be eligible for OSAP (or, for BSWD, an institution-funded special bursary). The page still links application forms only for 2023-24 and 2024-25. See also canada-student-grant-services-equipment.

entries.name: Submit a complaint about child welfare services (Government of Ontario)
entries.description: An Ontario government page explaining how to complain about a children's aid society (including an Indigenous society): to the society's Internal Complaints Review Panel, to the Child and Family Services Review Board (an independent tribunal), or at any time to the Ontario Ombudsman. It sets out the forms, deadlines and timelines for each route.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention any fee.
entries.evidence: The Child and Family Services Review Board (CFSRB) is an independent tribunal that can review certain service-related complaints related to children’s aid societies.
entries.notes: CNAF lists it on its national page; it serves Ontario only. The phone number is the Ontario Ombudsman's and the email is the Child and Family Services Review Board's (which takes forms by mail, email or fax, within 10 calendar days of the society's notice). Page updated April 20, 2026.

entries.name: For the Love of a Child
entries.description: A volunteer-run charity in Durham Region, Ontario, that helps families of children with special needs pay for specialized equipment and therapy that government funding and private insurance do not fully cover, for example assistive devices only partly paid for by ADP. The child must live in Durham Region, be under 21 and have a formal diagnosis; requests are reviewed every 2 months.
entries.cost_note: A funding charity; the site does not mention any cost to apply. It does not fund respite.
entries.evidence: For the Love of a Child contributes to the costs of various services and equipment.
entries.notes: CNAF lists it on its national page; it serves Durham Region, Ontario only, and its mailing address is a PO box in Oshawa. The latest copyright date on the site is 2020, but the online application form is live.

entries.name: Geneva Centre for Autism
entries.description: A Toronto charity with programs for autistic children, teens and adults: ABA, IBI and social skills programs for children and teens; life skills, employment, respite and social groups for adults; and camps and respite for all ages. It also offers training and consultation for organizations and hosts an autism symposium in Toronto.
entries.cost_note: Children's and teens' programs are accepted by the OAP; adult programs accept (DSO) Passport funding.
entries.evidence: Our flexible client-led and evidence-backed programs enable individuals with autism to live, work, and engage within their communities.
entries.notes: CNAF links to two Geneva Centre training pages on autism.net (an online ABA course for educators and its training institute); autism.net now redirects to genevacentre.ca, where those pages return 404, so this entry is for the organisation. Other centres: 164 Merton St. and 3036 Danforth Ave. Its Adult Social Club program is already in scripts/data/services/nd_mentoring.json (geneva-centre-adult-social-club); the organisation itself is not.

entries.name: Autism Program (McMaster Children's Hospital)
entries.description: McMaster Children's Hospital's program for autistic children and youth up to 18 (some services to 21) in Hamilton, Burlington, Oakville, Brantford, Niagara and nearby areas. It offers Ontario Autism Program services (foundational family services, caregiver-mediated early years, entry to school, school support, urgent response) and fee-based ABA, occupational therapy, speech-language and mental health services; the hospital is also the West Region autism diagnostic hub.
entries.cost_note: Foundational family services, early years and entry to school programs are free for OAP-registered families; core clinical services are fee-based (OAP funding, out of pocket, community funding or private insurance).
entries.evidence: Our services are available to autistic children and youth up to the age of 18, with some services available for young adults up to age 21.
entries.notes: CNAF lists Chedoke Child and Family Centre (Hamilton/Niagara region lead) and the Hamilton-Niagara Regional Autism Intervention Program, linking to mcmasterchildrenshospital.ca/body.cfm?id=65 and hamiltonhealthsciences.ca/sites/ccfc/pdd.htm (both 404) and a .doc on cnaf.net; this is McMaster Children's Hospital's current autism program page. Based at Ron Joyce Children's Health Centre; children need an autism diagnosis first. A different program at that centre is already in scripts/data/services/early_years.json (ron-joyce-developmental-pediatrics-rehabilitation).

entries.name: Autism Services (CHEO)
entries.description: CHEO's ABA-based services for children and youth with autism in Eastern Ontario: early intervention for children 12 to 42 months, foundational family services (workshops and brief consultations), school support services for children and youth up to 18, urgent response services and Social ABCs. CHEO's Diagnostic Assessment Team also offers diagnosis and assessment.
entries.cost_note: The FAQ says all of CHEO's autism services can be purchased with an OAP Childhood Budget; registration starts with a free phone consultation.
entries.evidence: At CHEO, we provide many resources and support services to help children, youth, and families navigate this journey.
entries.notes: CNAF lists CHEO as the Eastern region lead (cheo.on.ca home page) and links to CHEO's Autism Intervention, School Support and ABA program pages (cheo.on.ca/en/autism, /ibi, /ssp, /ABA), which now return 404; this is CHEO's current Autism Services page. Clinical locations: Beaverbrook Road and Industrial Avenue (Ottawa), Cornwall and Renfrew. The FAQ says CHEO is waiting for a new provincial needs-based program before deciding its long-term offerings; other CHEO programs are already in scripts/data/services/early_years.json (cheo-childrens-treatment-centre, cheo-school-based-rehabilitation).

entries.name: Autism Services (Surrey Place)
entries.description: Surrey Place's autism services in Toronto for children, youth and adults: autism diagnosis and assessment, OAP-eligible therapy (one-to-one, group and virtual ABA, and summer camp), free school transition and urgent response services, and other free services for families without funding or a diagnosis.
entries.cost_note: Therapy can be paid with OAP funding, insurance or out of pocket; school transition, urgent response and some other autism services are free.
entries.evidence: Discover personalized autism services, from speech and occupational therapy to ABA and mental health support
entries.notes: CNAF lists Surrey Place Centre (Toronto region lead) and links to an old IBI brochure PDF on abacuslist.ca, which no longer loads; the organisation's own site is surreyplace.ca. Locations: downtown Toronto, North York, Etobicoke and Scarborough; adult services: 1-855-DS ADULT (372-3858). Other Surrey Place programs are already in scripts/data/services/early_years.json (surrey-place-smartstart-hub, toronto-preschool-speech-language-surrey-place, surrey-place-infant-child-development); its autism services page is not.

entries.name: Autism and Behavioural Services (Hands TheFamilyHelpNetwork.ca)
entries.description: Bilingual services for children and youth with autism and their families in Northeastern Ontario: core clinical services (ABA and speech-language therapy), Project ImPACT coaching for parents of children 12 to 48 months, the Entry to School program, foundational family services, community clinic days and enhanced respite funding. Services are offered in person at offices across the region and virtually.
entries.cost_note: Foundational family services, Entry to School and community clinic days are free; the page does not list fees for core clinical services.
entries.evidence: We have been providing bilingual Autism and Behavioural Services in Northeastern Ontario for over 20 years.
entries.notes: CNAF lists Algonquin Child and Family Services (North East region lead) and links to dsontario.ca; Hands' About page says Algonquin Child and Family Services took the name Hands TheFamilyHelpNetwork.ca in 2008. The dsontario.ca link is Developmental Services Ontario, which is already in scripts/data/services/funding.json as developmental-services-ontario. Address is the North Bay office; the site's email addresses are hidden.

entries.name: Autism Services (Maltby Centre)
entries.description: Maltby Centre's autism services for children and youth in Kingston, Frontenac and Lennox & Addington: free OAP-funded programs (foundational family services, Project ImPACT, urgent response services, the Autism Behavioural Classroom and school support programs) and client-funded core clinical services such as ABA therapy and psychotherapy.
entries.cost_note: OAP-funded programs are free; core clinical services (ABA, psychotherapy) have fees and are eligible OAP Core Clinical expenses.
entries.evidence: Maltby Centre offers both OAP Funded and Client Funded Autism Core Clinical Services.
entries.notes: CNAF links to pathwayschildrenyouth.org; that no longer works. The organisation now uses maltbycentre.ca: its history page says it was established as Pathways for Children & Youth in 1996 and renamed Maltby Centre in 2018. Not the same as Pathways Health Centre for Children (Sarnia) in scripts/data/services/early_years.json. Other offices: Napanee, Harrowsmith, Sharbot Lake and Northbrook.

entries.name: Autism & Behavioural Services (Thames Valley Children's Centre)
entries.description: Thames Valley Children's Centre's services for children and youth with autism and their families in the 10 counties of Southwestern Ontario: free foundational family services, caregiver-mediated early years (ages 1-4) and entry to school (ages 3-6) programs by invitation, and individual and group core clinical services with eligible funding.
entries.cost_note: Foundational Family Services are at no cost; Core Clinical Services may be purchased with OAP funding, other MCCSS sources or Jordan's Principle funds.
entries.evidence: At TVCC, Autism & Behavioural Services (ABS) has been providing services to children and youth with autism/ASD and their families for 25 years in Southwestern Ontario.
entries.notes: CNAF lists TVCC twice (South West region lead, and again under ABA service providers), linking to tvcc.on.ca; this is its current autism services page. Families can book a free 'Talk With Me' consultation. Other TVCC programs are already in scripts/data/services/early_years.json (tvcc-smartstart-hub, tyketalk-thames-valley); its autism services page is not.

entries.name: Autism Services (Kinark Child and Family Services)
entries.description: Kinark's services for children and youth with autism aged 2 to 18 and their families, mainly in York Region, Durham Region and Simcoe County: ABA coaching; centre-based, home-based, virtual and group ABA; Connections for Students school transition support; foundational family services (including programs for siblings and parents); caregiver-mediated early years; and the Entry to School program.
entries.cost_note: Foundational Family Services are free for families registered in the OAP; the site does not list fees for other services.
entries.evidence: Services are provided throughout the Greater Toronto Area, primarily in York Region, Durham Region, and Simcoe County, to children and youth aged two to 18, and their families.
entries.notes: CNAF lists Kinark (Central East region lead) and links to kinark.on.ca/services/Default.aspx, which returns 404; this is Kinark's current autism page (it also links a separate site, kinarkautismservices.ca). Autism Services phone from the Contact Us page.

entries.name: Ontario Association for Behaviour Analysis (ONTABA)
entries.description: Ontario's professional association for behaviour analysis, an affiliate chapter of the Association for Behaviour Analysis International. It runs events, shares reports and resources on the regulation of ABA in Ontario and posts jobs; it is not a regulator or a certification body.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost on these pages (it has paid membership sign-up).
entries.evidence: ONTABA is a professional association, not a regulatory body nor a certification body.
entries.notes: A professional association for practitioners (members from education, nursing, health care and psychology), not a service provider; families may find its ABA and regulation information useful. Address (Suite 500) from the Contact page; no phone or general email is listed.

entries.name: Behaviour Innovations
entries.description: A private ABA provider serving Hamilton, Oakville, Etobicoke, London and nearby areas. It offers autism diagnosis and psychoeducational assessments, ABA and IBI for children, social groups, tutoring, parent coaching, and adult and teen programs, in centre, at home or virtually.
entries.cost_note: The FAQ says OAP core clinical funding can be used for ABA programs and Passport funds toward the Hub day program's daily fee.
entries.evidence: Behaviour Innovations has been a leading provider of individualized Applied Behaviour Analytic (ABA) services since 1998 throughout Hamilton, Oakville, Etobicoke, London and nearby areas.
entries.notes: CNAF lists Behaviour Institute; behaviourinstitute.com now redirects to behaviourinnovations.com. The site does not mention the old name, so a reviewer may want to confirm it is the same organisation. Phone and address are the Hamilton office; the Toronto office is at 618 The Queensway, (416) 251-9277. Diagnostic assessments are for ages 18 months through adulthood (FAQ).

entries.name: Beyond The Door Behaviour Associates
entries.description: A Toronto ABA/IBI provider for children with autism and other developmental delays, with therapy at its centre, at home, at daycare or at school, plus parent training and behaviour management. It is OAP approved and serves both private and funded clients.
entries.cost_note: Serves private and funded (OAP) clients; offers a free first consultation at home.
entries.evidence: Beyond The Door is a Team of dedicated Professionals with over 20 years experience providing ABA services for children with developmental delays and learning disabilities including Autism Spectrum Disorder.
entries.notes: CNAF lists it twice (Beyond the Door, and Beyond the Door Behaviour Associates); one link (index.php?p=144) returns 404, the home page works. Address is the BTD Learning Centre (the Leslie St address is mailing only).

entries.name: Exceptional Learning Centre
entries.description: A centre in Ajax with a small-class private school program, 1:1 ABA therapy, speech-language therapy, parent coaching, social skills groups, ABA-based tutoring and a summer program for children and youth with autism, ADHD, communication disorders, learning disabilities and other neurodevelopmental needs.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Individualized education and support for children with neurodevelopmental diagnoses and unique learning needs.
entries.notes: CNAF links to exlcentre.com (now https://exlcentre.com/). Contact details from the home page.

entries.name: Missing Links
entries.description: A Burlington ABA centre and academy with ABA programs for children aged 2 to 14, social groups, tutoring and executive functioning sessions, a part-time or full-time adult program, online courses for families and professionals, and remote services, including for Northern Ontario.
entries.cost_note: The site says programs can be paid through funding or privately.
entries.evidence: At Missing Links, we offer ABA programming for clients 2–14 years old.
entries.notes: CNAF links to missinglinks.ca (now https://www.missinglinks.ca/). Programs are developed and supervised by a BCBA; the site offers help getting on its waiting list.

entries.name: Shining Through Centre for Children with Autism
entries.description: A registered charity offering ABA-based therapy, education and support for children and youth with autism from 18 months to 21 years and their families, at centres in Woodbridge, North York and Mississauga. Services include assessment and diagnosis, ABA/IBI, inclusion and youth programs, parent coaching, tutoring, social clubs and camps.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: We provide therapy, education, and support to children and youth with autism, and their families.
entries.notes: CNAF links to shiningthrough.ca (now https://www.shiningthrough.ca/). Ages and the three centres from the Contact page; the North York centre is at 250 Beecroft Road, the address CNAF gives for 'Beecroft Learning Centre'.

entries.name: The Joy of Learning · Burloak Academy
entries.description: A private early learning school that combines ABA, speech-language therapy, occupational therapy and modified Ontario Curriculum teaching, set in Bronte Creek Provincial Park. It focuses on communication, behaviour, social and academic skills for young children.
entries.cost_note: Programs (except the School Readiness Academy) are eligible for OAP reimbursement; SLP and OT may be covered by personal insurance.
entries.evidence: We are an early learning environment offering Child Development and Private Educational services through Applied Behaviour Analysis (ABA), Speech Language Pathology (SLP), Occupational Therapy (OT), and modified Ontario Curriculum educational services.
entries.notes: CNAF lists The Joy of Learning Centre at jolc.ca, which now presents itself as The Joy of Learning · Burloak Academy. The site gives no street address: it is in Tyrell House, Bronte Creek Provincial Park (entrance from Burloak Dr.). The latest blog post is dated March 2025.

entries.name: Jordan's Principle (Six Nations Department of Well-Being)
entries.description: The Jordan's Principle team at Six Nations of the Grand River helps First Nations children and their families apply for Jordan's Principle funding when a child has an unmet health, social or educational need. Navigators complete the intake form with families, receive the supporting documents for a request, link families to community resources and follow up after a request.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention a fee for the team's help; approved Jordan's Principle requests are paid for by government.
entries.evidence: The Jordan’s Principle team at Six Nations provides support with funding requests and service delivery related to unmet health, social and educational needs.
entries.notes: The federal Jordan's Principle program is already in scripts/data/services/funding.json as jordans-principle; this is the local Six Nations team that helps families apply. Referrals in person at the Child and Youth Health office (White Pines Wellness Centre), by phone or by fax (519-445-4783), Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. Children must be under 18 in Ontario and meet the program's First Nations criteria. Footer shows © 2022.

entries.name: Ontario child care fee subsidy and Special Needs Resourcing (SNR)
entries.description: Ontario families can apply, through their local municipal service manager, District Social Services Administration Board or First Nations band office, for help paying for licensed child care, children's recreation programs, camps or board-run before and after school programs, based on family income. The same page describes Special Needs Resourcing, which pays for staff, equipment and other supports so children with special needs can take part in licensed child care, EarlyON centres, recreation programs and camps at no extra cost to parents.
entries.cost_note: What a family pays for child care depends on its adjusted net income; Special Needs Resourcing is provided at no additional cost to parents.
entries.evidence: Families can apply for the Ontario child care fee subsidy. The cost of this program is shared by the Ontario government, municipal governments and First Nation communities.
entries.notes: Apply through the local Consolidated Municipal Service Manager (CMSM), District Social Services Administration Board (DSSAB) or First Nations band office; the page gives no phone or email. CNAF also links to the old edu.gov.on.ca/childcare/paying.html page, which now shows Page Not Found; this ontario.ca page covers the same subsidy. Children are eligible under 13, or up to 18 if they have special needs and entered child care before August 31, 2017. Page updated October 22, 2025.

entries.name: The Job Centre
entries.description: An employment service for youth and adults with physical disabilities, mental health conditions, autism, learning disabilities, hearing loss or visual impairment in Halton, Peel, Guelph and Waterloo Region. Case managers and job developers help set job goals, prepare resumes and interviews, place people in jobs and provide job coaching and a year of follow-up, and they can help pay for work clothing, equipment or transportation needed for a job.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost; it says the service is funded through Integrated Employment Services in Halton.
entries.evidence: The Job Centre provides a range of employment supports to youth and adults with physical, mental health, autism spectrum disorder, learning disabilities, hard of hearing and visual impairment.
entries.notes: Contact details from the Contact Us page (toll free 1-800-350-8361; Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 5 pm). The only email shown is the director's own address, so none is given. Staff travel to meet clients near home and have meeting space by appointment in each city served. Footer says © 2020.

entries.name: PATH Employment Services
entries.description: A Hamilton non-profit that has helped people with any kind of disability find and keep jobs since 1972. Members work one on one with an employment coordinator on an action plan that can include career assessments, resumes, job search and follow-up after a placement, and they can use a free Employment Resource Centre with computers, job sites and accessibility software.
entries.cost_note: The Employment Resource Centre is free for members; one-on-one help is an Employment Ontario program funded by the Ontario government.
entries.address: 501-12 James St North, Hamilton ON, L8R2J9
entries.evidence: PATH is a non-profit agency that has been helping people with any kind of disability get and keep jobs since 1972.
entries.notes: Contact details from the Contact Us page; TTY users can call through Bell Relay (711). With Centre3 it also runs 360 [4] Youth, training and a subsidized work placement for ages 15 to 30, and the site lists ACTION Niagara. The site says its workshops are being revamped.

entries.name: Ontario Disability Employment Network (ODEN)
entries.description: A province-wide network of more than 140 employment service providers that help people with disabilities get into the workforce. It works with businesses on inclusive hiring, trains and speaks up for service providers, and lists its member agencies with their contact details on a Find a Member page.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention any cost for job seekers.
entries.address: 4081 Thickson Road North Whitby, ON L1R 2X0
entries.evidence: The Ontario Disability Employment Network (ODEN) is a province-wide organization that brings together businesses and Employment Service Providers to increase employment opportunities for job seekers who have a disability.
entries.notes: Contact details from the Contact page (office in Whitby). French-language help is referred to member Performance Plus at 1-800-427-6214. The site lists a Rethinking Disability Conference 2026 and a 2024–2025 annual report. The Job Centre (also on this sheet) says it is an ODEN member.

entries.name: Easter Seals Ontario
entries.description: A charity for children, youth and young adults in Ontario with physical disabilities, such as cerebral palsy, spina bifida or muscular dystrophy, and their families. It runs two accessible summer camps, funds mobility and accessibility equipment, offers scholarships and an ambassador program, and runs the provincially funded Incontinence Supplies Grant and Top Up programs.
entries.cost_note: Charity; the pages fetched do not list fees. Equipment funding is up to $3,000 per child per year.
entries.address: One Concorde Gate, Suite 700, Toronto, ON M3C 3N6
entries.evidence: Easter Seals Ontario is a registered charitable organization that supports children, youth, and young adults with physical disabilities from all backgrounds.
entries.notes: Its Equipment Funding Program is already in scripts/data/services/funding.json as easter-seals-ontario-equipment-funding; this entry is the organisation as a whole. The camps are Camp Woodeden and Camp Merrywood (camp@easterseals.org). The services.easterseals.org pages could not be fetched today (TLS error), so details come from the About and Contact pages. It serves physical disabilities, not autism as such.

entries.name: Special Supports Program (City of Hamilton)
entries.description: A City of Hamilton program that helps people on Ontario Works or ODSP and other low-income adult residents pay for health-related items such as bath and toilet aids, dentures and dental care, eyeglasses, diabetic supplies and emergency response systems. A note from a doctor or health professional is usually needed, and funding must be approved before anything is ordered or bought.
entries.cost_note: Benefit program; the page does not mention a fee to apply. It does not pay for items already ordered or bought.
entries.evidence: Hamilton low income residents may be eligible to receive medical benefits under this program if their household income falls below the Statistics Canada Low Income Measure.
entries.notes: CNAF links to hamilton.ca/social-services/support-programs/special-supports-program, which returns 404. The program is now at this hamilton.ca page (modified August 12, 2026). Apply online at specialsupportsbenefits.hamilton.ca, by phone (8:30 am to 4 pm weekdays) or with a paper form; the email address is hidden on the page. Low-income applicants must be 18 or older, live in Hamilton, not be on OW or ODSP and be under the income limits.

entries.name: Community Living Hamilton
entries.description: A Hamilton agency for people with an intellectual or developmental disability and their families. Its services include community participation programs, supported group and independent living, respite for adults and for children and youth, child care supports, Passport fund management, Special Services at Home and employment services.
entries.cost_note: Many services are reached by referral (for example from Developmental Services Ontario); others are paid for by the person or family, with Passport or Special Services at Home funding or out of pocket.
entries.evidence: Whether you live with an intellectual or developmental disability – or care for someone who does – you will find supports that suit your needs at Community Living Hamilton.
entries.notes: CNAF links to communitylivinghamilton.com/services, which now redirects to the Services & Supports page. Referrals also come through Contact Hamilton or the City of Hamilton. Contact details from the Contact Us page; no email is shown (contact form only).

entries.name: Ontario Drug Benefit (ODB) program
entries.description: An Ontario program that pays most of the cost of more than 5,900 prescription drugs on its formulary, plus some diabetes test strips, nutrition products and allergy shots. It covers people 65 and older, people 24 and younger without private insurance (through OHIP+), people receiving Ontario Works or ODSP, people in long-term care or getting home and community care, and people enrolled in the Trillium Drug Program.
entries.cost_note: People on Ontario Works or ODSP pay up to $2 per prescription with no deductible (nothing if 24 or under); seniors pay a $100 yearly deductible and up to $6.11 per prescription unless in the Seniors Co-Payment Program.
entries.evidence: The Ontario Drug Benefit program covers most of the cost of more than 5,900 medications listed on the ODB Formulary and almost 1,500 additional drug products that meet specific criteria through the Exceptional Access Program (EAP).
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old health.gov.on.ca drug program forms page (opdp_forms.aspx); that domain no longer resolves. The program is now at this ontario.ca page (updated August 18, 2026). The phone is the ODB program line for questions (416-503-4586 in Toronto; seniors@ontariodrugbenefit.ca); the Trillium Drug Program, for high drug costs, is 1-800-575-5386. People on ODSP or Ontario Works are covered automatically; prescriptions must be filled in Ontario.

entries.name: Community pass and Access pass (OC Transpo)
entries.description: Reduced-fare transit passes in Ottawa. The Community pass lets Ottawa residents who receive ODSP ride OC Transpo buses, the O-Train and Para Transpo for about half the regular fare, and the Access pass, at the same price, is for registered Para Transpo customers who also use regular buses and trains.
entries.cost_note: Community pass: $1.75 per ride or $43.25 a month (2026 fares); the Access pass is $43.25 a month plus a $2.75 top-up per Para Transpo ride.
entries.evidence: The Community pass is available to Ontario Disability Support Program (ODSP) recipients and offers a reduced fare on single-ride and monthly passes.
entries.notes: CNAF links to octranspo.com/tickets-and-passes/community_pass, which now redirects to the general Fares page; the passes are now at /en/fares/reduced-fares/community-pass/ and /access-pass/. Apply by phone (the Access pass also by mail, fax or in person); a Presto card registered in the applicant's name is needed. The Community pass no longer needs renewing while the person gets ODSP, up to age 65.

entries.name: Special Needs Planning Group
entries.description: An Ontario planning group, started in 1997 by the father of a daughter with a disability, that helps families plan the financial future of a relative with a disability without losing benefits such as ODSP, using tools like Henson Trusts, the RDSP and life insurance. Its Trustee Support Program helps trustees of Henson Trusts in Ontario with ODSP rules, record keeping and tax returns.
entries.cost_note: The site offers free personalized guidance and a complimentary planning session; insurance and investment products are offered separately (investment advice through Optimize Wealth Management Inc.).
entries.evidence: Founded in 1997, our mission is to help families create secure, sustainable financial plans that preserve access to government benefits.
entries.notes: CNAF links to specialneedsplanning.ca/about.html and /henson.html (What is a Trust), which return 404; the current site is specialneedsplanning.ca (© 2026, June 2026 update). A notice on the site says they are temporarily unable to respond to emails and the site is an informational resource for now; the Contact page returns 404 and no phone or email is shown. The founder is retiring and has passed leadership to Ken and Ryan White.

entries.name: Office of the Public Guardian and Trustee (OPGT)
entries.description: An Ontario government office that makes financial decisions for adults found mentally incapable, acts as substitute decision-maker of last resort for treatment and long-term care decisions, and investigates when an incapable person may be at risk of harm. Its pages explain powers of attorney (with a free kit), guardianship, and how a spouse, partner or relative can apply to replace the OPGT as guardian of property.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention fees, apart from saying the power of attorney kit is free.
entries.evidence: acts as Substitute Decision Maker (SDM) of last resort to make substitute treatment or long-term care admission decisions for incapable individuals
entries.notes: CNAF links to old attorneygeneral.jus.gov.on.ca/english/family/pgt/incapacity/ pages on mental incapacity, planning ahead, powers of attorney and guardianship; they all now redirect to the Ministry of the Attorney General home page. The OPGT is now at this ontario.ca page (updated September 15, 2026), which links to its Mental capacity, Make a power of attorney and Guardianship pages. Regional offices in Toronto, London, Sudbury, Thunder Bay, Hamilton and Ottawa; the same toll-free number is the Investigations line.

entries.name: Capacity Assessment Office (Ministry of the Attorney General)
entries.description: Ontario's Capacity Assessment Office trains capacity assessors, who formally assess whether a person can make decisions about property or personal care, and gives financial help to people who cannot afford an assessment. Families arrange an assessment directly with an assessor from the province's list; financial help applies when only a designated assessor can do the assessment and the person will not refuse it.
entries.cost_note: Assessors set their own hourly or flat fees, usually paid by the person who asks for the assessment; financial assistance is available to those who cannot afford it and meet the financial criteria.
entries.evidence: You can get financial assistance to cover the cost of an assessment if you cannot afford the fees.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old attorneygeneral.jus.gov.on.ca PGT capacity assessment page, which now redirects to the Ministry of the Attorney General home page; capacity assessment is now explained on this ontario.ca Mental capacity page (updated September 8, 2025). Financial Assistance Application forms go to the office by email, phone or mail, and it replies within 10 business days; CAO@ontario.ca is the office's own address and mail goes to 595 Bay Street, 8th Floor, Toronto. Financial help is not available to people who are already clients of the Public Guardian and Trustee.

entries.name: Guardianship (Office of the Public Guardian and Trustee)
entries.description: A guardian makes decisions for an adult who is mentally incapable of making certain decisions: a guardian of property is appointed by Ontario's Office of the Public Guardian and Trustee (OPGT) or the Superior Court of Justice, and a guardian of the person by the court. A spouse, partner or relative can apply to replace the OPGT as guardian of property, and the OPGT investigates concerns about incapable people at serious risk.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention fees; it suggests speaking with a lawyer before a court application.
entries.evidence: If the OPGT already serves as guardian of property for the incapable person, you can apply to replace the OPGT.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old attorneygeneral.jus.gov.on.ca 'Becoming a Guardian' page; that now redirects to the Ministry of the Attorney General home page. The program is now at https://www.ontario.ca/page/guardianship (updated May 13, 2025). The phone is the OPGT toll-free line from the OPGT page, which also lists regional offices (Toronto, London, Sudbury, Thunder Bay, Hamilton, Ottawa) and their emails. A different program from the ontario.ca services already in ResourceHub. Ontario_part1 item 56 links to the same old page: merge if that draft keeps it too.

entries.name: Estates Law (Nelligan Law)
entries.description: Nelligan Law is an Ottawa law firm whose estates team prepares wills and powers of attorney, sets up trusts (including for dependants with disabilities or people with special needs), and helps with estate administration and disputes. It sees clients at its Ottawa office and by virtual consultation across Ontario.
entries.cost_note: Fixed pricing for simple estate planning (a will and powers of attorney): $1,450 for an individual, $1,750 for a couple; complex trusts are add-ons.
entries.evidence: Trusts – For minors, dependants with disabilities, long-term planning, or tax-efficient management of assets.
entries.notes: CNAF links to an old nelligan.ca article ('Handle with Care - Who can Make Decisions for your Disabled Adult Children?'); it now redirects to the Nelligan Law home page, which links a current post, 'Planning for an Adult Child with a Disability in Ontario'. Address and phone from the Contact page (firm name Nelligan O’Brien Payne LLP); its email address is hidden, so email is null. Private law firm; fees apply.

entries.name: JusticeNet
entries.description: JusticeNet is a not-for-profit organization that helps people who cannot afford standard legal fees, but do not qualify for legal aid, find Ontario lawyers, paralegals and mediators who charge reduced hourly rates based on income. The legal matter must be in Ontario.
entries.cost_note: One-time $25 registration plus tax (not charged if personal net income is below $25,000); reduced hourly rates paid to the professional, e.g. lawyers $130–$200/hr.
entries.evidence: JusticeNet helps people facing financial difficulties find Ontario lawyers, paralegals and mediators who offer reduced fees.
entries.notes: CNAF's link (justicenet.ca/about-us/) redirects to the current About page. Income guideline: under $70,000 for a household of 1 or 2, under $90,000 for 3 or more; the legal matter must be in Ontario (the person can live elsewhere), so this is an Ontario entry. Contact details from the Contact page; the Thornhill office is not open to the public and the call centre cannot search the directory or give legal advice.

entries.name: Hamilton Community Legal Clinic
entries.description: A community legal clinic funded by Legal Aid Ontario that gives legal help to low-income residents anywhere in the City of Hamilton, in areas such as housing, social assistance and employment. Its ODSP service helps people who were refused the Ontario Disability Support Program, or whose benefits were reduced, cancelled or suspended, to challenge the decision and appeal to the Social Benefits Tribunal.
entries.cost_note: The site does not state a fee; it says the clinic is funded by Legal Aid Ontario and serves low-income Hamilton residents.
entries.evidence: If you have applied for ODSP benefits and have been turned down, we can assist you in appealing this decision and building your case.
entries.notes: CNAF's two links (hamiltonjustice.ca/about-us.php and /ontario-disability-support-program.php) return 404; the clinic is current at https://hamiltonjustice.ca/en/ (news posted September 2026), and this one entry covers both CNAF items. Serves low-income residents of the City of Hamilton only; apply online or by phone. Address and phone from the Contact page.

entries.name: Henson Trust planning (DH Professional Corporation)
entries.description: DH Professional Corporation is a Mississauga law firm that advises on wills and estate planning. Its Henson Trust service sets up an absolute discretionary trust in parents' wills so that an inheritance left to a child or adult with a disability does not affect their ODSP benefits.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: DH Professional Corporation can advise clients on will and estate planning or litigation and dispute resolution associated with a will or estate.
entries.notes: CNAF's link is current (page footer © 2011 - 2026). The site's https certificate does not verify, so the http address is kept. Address and phone from the Contact page (toll free 1.877.273.3339); the only emails listed are the two lawyers' own, so email is null. Private law firm.

entries.name: Special Needs Planning (O’Sullivan Estate Lawyers LLP)
entries.description: O’Sullivan Estate Lawyers LLP is a Toronto law firm that practises only trust and estate law. Its special needs planning includes powers of attorney and guardianships, inter vivos trusts, Henson and other special needs trusts, and help setting up Registered Disability Savings Plans, so families can provide for a child or adult with a disability without affecting their government benefits.
entries.cost_note: Fees are based mainly on time spent; the minimum fee for estate planning (a will and two powers of attorney) starts at $5,000 plus HST and disbursements.
entries.evidence: We can help you manage children’s inheritance funds, and ensure that minors and adults with serious injuries and disabilities, or with Asperger’s syndrome, autism, ADHD and other illnesses and challenges receive the financial protection and support they need.
entries.notes: CNAF has five links to this firm (special needs planning, Margaret O'Sullivan's profile, firm overview, living trusts, guardianship and management plans); this one entry covers them. The old .shtml addresses redirect to current pages, except the Margaret O'Sullivan profile, which now returns 404. Founded in 1998; address and phone from the page footer, fees from the Engagement and Fees page; contact is by phone or web form (no email shown).

entries.name: Justice for Children and Youth (JFCY)
entries.description: Justice for Children and Youth is a non-profit legal aid clinic, based in Toronto, whose staff lawyers represent and advocate for young people under 18, and unstably housed youth under 25, across Ontario. It gives free summary legal advice by phone on problems with the legal, education, social service or mental health systems, including advice to parents on education matters.
entries.cost_note: Up to 30 minutes of free summary legal advice by phone; further help and representation for those who meet its eligibility guidelines (part of Legal Aid Ontario's poverty law clinics).
entries.evidence: Justice for Children and Youth (JFCY) has staff lawyers who represent and advocate for youth under 18 and unstably housed youth under 25.
entries.notes: CNAF's link (http://www.jfcy.org/) redirects to https://jfcy.org/en/. Eligibility: under 18, or under 25 and homeless, in Ontario (so 18-30 is only for unstably housed youth up to 25); no civil lawsuits and generally no family law. Contact details from the Contact page: intake is by phone (GTA 416-920-1633), there are no walk-in services, and the email inbox is not for legal advice.

entries.name: Special education (Ontario Ministry of Education)
entries.description: Ontario school boards must provide special education programs and services, from kindergarten to Grade 12 in publicly funded schools, for students with special education needs such as autism and learning, intellectual or physical disabilities. Parents work with the child's teacher, principal and school board on assessment, the identification, placement and review committee (IPRC), an individual education plan (IEP) and transition planning, with placements from a regular class with support to a full-time special education class.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost; it covers special education in publicly funded schools.
entries.evidence: By law, all school boards must provide special education programs and/or services for students with special education needs.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old edu.gov.on.ca special education pages (eng/general/elemsec/speced/speced.html and eng/parents/speced.html); both now show 'Page Not Found'. The program is now at https://www.ontario.ca/page/special-education (updated September 1, 2026), with sub-pages on the IPRC and IEPs; this one entry covers both CNAF items, and is a different program from the ontario.ca services already in ResourceHub. No central contact: families start with the child's teacher or principal, then the school board's student and family support office.

entries.name: Ontario Human Rights Commission (OHRC)
entries.description: An arm's-length Ontario government agency that works to prevent discrimination and promote human rights under the Ontario Human Rights Code, through education, policy development, public inquiries and litigation. It does not give advice on individual cases; discrimination claims are filed with the Human Rights Tribunal of Ontario, and the Human Rights Legal Support Centre gives free legal help.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost for the OHRC itself; it says the Human Rights Legal Support Centre gives free legal assistance.
entries.evidence: The Ontario Human Rights Commission (OHRC) was established as an arm’s length agency of government in 1961 to prevent discrimination and to promote and advance human rights in Ontario.
entries.notes: CNAF links to an OHRC paper on the Safe Schools Act and school discipline (still online); this entry is for the Commission itself. Its contact page says it cannot advise on individual cases and points people to the HRLSC (free legal help) and the HRTO (where claims are filed). Office: 180 Dundas Street West, 9th Floor, Toronto; local phone (416) 326-9511. Other Ontario sheets also link OHRC pages, so check for a duplicate.

entries.name: Community Integration Through Co-operative Education (CICE) (Fanshawe College)
entries.description: A two-year Ontario College Certificate program at Fanshawe College in London for students with developmental disabilities, acquired brain injuries, intellectual disabilities and other significant learning challenges. Students take core CICE courses and one area of concentration (such as culinary, photography, recreation, early childhood education, horticulture or office administration) with support from Learning Facilitators, and complete three field placements.
entries.cost_note: Total program cost for Canadian students is listed as about $10,092.52 (approximate; includes a MacBook), plus other fees.
entries.evidence: The CICE program is a two-year Ontario College Certificate program designed for students with developmental disabilities, acquired brain injuries, intellectual disabilities and other significant learning challenges.
entries.notes: CNAF's link redirects to the current program page (code CIT2). Starts September 2026 and September 2027 at the London campus, domestic applicants only; apply on ontariocolleges.ca (February 1 for selection), then an advocate reference form, resume and interview, with a waiting list when full. No program phone or email on the page. Fanshawe's accessibility, tutoring and mentoring services are separate ResourceHub listings; this is a different program.

entries.name: Community Integration through Co-operative Education (CICE) (Mohawk College)
entries.description: A two-year Ontario College Certificate program at Mohawk College's Fennell Campus in Hamilton for students with intellectual disabilities and other significant learning challenges. Students take modified core and elective courses with individualized support, complete two unpaid work placements, and build a transition plan for employment, education, independence and recreation; there are May and September intakes.
entries.cost_note: 2026-2027 domestic first-year tuition and fees total $4,460.13; books and supplies are extra.
entries.evidence: This program offers students with intellectual disabilities and other significant learning challenges the opportunity to pursue a postsecondary education, prepare for success in entry level work, build independence and self-advocacy skills for adult life.
entries.notes: CNAF's old interdisciplinary-studies link redirects to this page. Admission needs proof of an intellectual disability and need for a modified curriculum (ODSP assessment, psycho-educational assessment or a doctor's note with an IEP), an intake package and an interview; students must get to campus on their own. Phone is Mohawk Admissions; the page gives the Learning Facilitators' email as cice [at] mohawkcollege.ca. Mohawk's accessible learning and learning support services are separate ResourceHub listings.

entries.name: Community Integration through Cooperative Education (CICE) (St. Clair College)
entries.description: A two-year Ontario College Certificate program at St. Clair College's Main Windsor Campus for people with developmental disabilities and other significant learning challenges. Students take CICE core courses (communications, job and life skills, human relations) and academic courses in a chosen vocational direction with support from a Learning Facilitator, and complete three field placements.
entries.cost_note: Standard college tuition and compulsory fees apply; placement travel, costs and extra screenings are the student's responsibility.
entries.evidence: This program is designed to provide individuals with developmental disabilities and other significant learning challenges with the opportunity to experience college life, pursue a postsecondary education and develop skills to help prepare them for employment or volunteer-work.
entries.notes: CNAF's old postsec/cice link redirects to this page (status Open, starts September). Admission requires a documented developmental disability, transportation to college and placements, and a supplementary application package with an interview; the intake is 25 students each fall and applying before February 1 is advised. Phone is the Main Windsor Campus line; the program contact listed is a named coordinator. St. Clair's accessibility, tutoring and student life services are separate ResourceHub listings.

entries.name: Community Integration Through Co-operative Education (CICE) (Georgian College)
entries.description: A two-year Ontario College Certificate program at Georgian College's Barrie and Owen Sound campuses for students with diverse learning challenges who need academic accommodations and modifications. Learning facilitators modify integrated courses and give tutoring and support, students complete three field placements, and some courses can be taken fully in person or fully online.
entries.cost_note: College tuition and fees apply (see Georgian's tuition and fees page); students must bring their own laptop.
entries.evidence: CICE is an inclusive and integrated postsecondary certificate program completed over two years and designed for learners who require additional academic support.
entries.notes: CNAF's link (academics/full-time-programs/...-cice/) returns a 308 redirect the fetcher cannot follow; the program was found through Georgian's program list and is now at /programs/community-integration-co-operative-education/. Next intake Fall 2027 at Barrie and Owen Sound (CNAF lists Barrie and Orillia). Admission needs OSSD/OSSC or age 19+, a demonstrated need for curriculum modification and an admissions interview. Georgian's accessibility advising, tutoring and peer mentor services are separate ResourceHub listings.

entries.name: Community Integration through Co-operative Education (CICE) (Humber Polytechnic)
entries.description: A four-semester Ontario College Certificate program at Humber Polytechnic's North Campus in Toronto for adults with intellectual disabilities who want to experience college life. Students take CICE courses and electives across Humber's faculties with individualized support, and complete community field placements, including a co-operative education placement; the program focuses on personal growth and independence rather than vocational training.
entries.cost_note: The 2026/2027 domestic fee for two semesters was $4,333.58; bursaries and scholarships are available.
entries.evidence: Humber Polytechnic's Community Integration through Co-operative Education (CICE) Ontario College Certificate program provides adults with intellectual disabilities the opportunity to experience college life in an inclusive and supportive post-secondary environment.
entries.notes: CNAF's humber.ca/program/... link is 404; the program is now at humber.ca/explore-programs/programs/community-integration-through-co-operative-education-cice (found in Humber's full-time program list). Applicants need a documented intellectual or developmental disability, must be 19 or older, and need an OSSC or Certificate of Achievement (or an OSSD plus a DSO letter); there are more applicants than spots. Next intake September 2027 at North campus. Humber's accessible learning, learning services and peer wellness are separate ResourceHub listings.

entries.name: Community Integration Through Co-operative Education (CICE) (Durham College)
entries.description: A two-year Ontario College Certificate program at Durham College's Oshawa campus for individuals with intellectual disabilities or significant learning challenges. Students take modified college courses in an area of interest plus CICE core courses (such as interpersonal communication, job skills and self-advocacy), with learning facilitators in class and a weekly tutorial, and complete three unpaid field placements.
entries.cost_note: College tuition applies (fee details on the page); OSAP, scholarships and bursaries may help.
entries.evidence: The Community Integration through Co-operative Education (CICE) program is designed for individuals with intellectual disabilities or significant learning challenges.
entries.notes: CNAF's link redirects to this page. Next intake September 2027 (open); applicants submit an additional application package and an online intake assessment, then an interview if selected. Phone is Durham's recruitment line for Canadian applicants; the CICE email is given for information sessions. Durham's Access and Support Centre and peer tutoring are separate ResourceHub listings.

entries.name: Community Integration Through Cooperative Education (CICE) (Fleming College)
entries.description: A two-year, in-person Ontario College Certificate program at Fleming College's Sutherland Campus in Peterborough for individuals with exceptionalities and other significant learning challenges. Students take courses modified to their learning needs to build skills for work, life and learning, and complete work placements.
entries.cost_note: Domestic tuition is listed at $2665.32 per semester (2026-2027); the program is OSAP-eligible and students can apply for bursaries.
entries.evidence: The Community Integration through Co-operative Education (CICE) program is designed to provide individuals with exceptionalities and other significant learning challenges the opportunity to experience college life and strengthen essential skills for work, life and learning.
entries.notes: CNAF's link loads this page. Next start September 7, 2027; apply on ontariocolleges.ca by February 1, then email a document of disability (such as proof of DSO or ODSP) and a document of academic needs (such as an IEP) to the program, followed by an interview. The page says Fleming is pursuing an amalgamation with St. Lawrence College (proposed for April 1, 2027), so the name may change. Fleming's accessible education and tutoring services are separate ResourceHub listings.

entries.name: Community Integration through Co-operative Education (CICE) (Lambton College)
entries.description: A two-year, in-person Ontario College Certificate program at Lambton College in Sarnia for students with learning or developmental disabilities, brain injuries and related learning challenges. Students choose an area of concentration from Lambton's programs and take modified courses with in-class support, weekly tutoring and job coaching from CICE staff, with field placements in three of the four terms.
entries.cost_note: Costs are listed as $4,250.34 for year 1 and $4,144.68 for year 2 (2026-2027), plus a police records check and health clearance.
entries.evidence: This program provides students with learning or developmental disabilities, brain injuries, and other related learning challenges, with opportunities to enhance their academic skills and develop vocational abilities.
entries.notes: CNAF's lambton.on.ca/CICE link redirects to lambtoncollege.ca. Limited enrolment: apply on ontariocolleges.ca (February 1 equal-consideration deadline), then scored interviews and references. Phone is the CICE program line; the page shows the program email ciceprogram@lambtoncollege.ca with a hidden character in it, so the general info@ address is used here. Lambton's Accessibility Centre and Lion's Mind are separate ResourceHub listings.

entries.name: Community Integration Through Cooperative Education (CICE) (Sault College)
entries.description: A two-year (four-semester) Ontario College Certificate program at Sault College in Sault Ste. Marie for students with learning challenges who need modifications to their curriculum. Students choose from 10 program areas of study paired with field placements, get in-class support and tutoring, and graduates work with an employment support specialist to find work.
entries.cost_note: 2026-2027 domestic fees for year 1: $2,701.10 tuition plus $1,274.00 ancillary fees.
entries.evidence: Community Integration through Cooperative Education (CICE) is a fully integrated two-year certificate program offering students with learning challenges, requiring modifications to their curriculum, more ways to enhance their academic, vocational and social skills.
entries.notes: CNAF's old Programs.asp link redirects to this page. Next start September 2027 (program code 1120); applicants apply on ontariocolleges.ca, complete a CICE admissions package and must arrange their own transportation. Phone is Sault College's main line; the program contact listed is a named person. Sault College's accessibility, peer tutoring and peer mentoring services are separate ResourceHub listings.

entries.name: Community Integration Through Co-operative Education (CICE) (Conestoga College)
entries.description: A two-year Ontario College Certificate program at Conestoga College's Kitchener – Doon campus for individuals with exceptionalities and other significant learning challenges. Students take core courses (such as human relations and communications, job skills, life skills and computer skills) and modified courses from other programs with support from Learning Strategists, and complete work placements.

entries.evidence: a two-year program designed to provide individuals with exceptionalities and other significant learning challenges the opportunity to experience college life and enhance their academic and vocational skills

Next start September 2027 (open); domestic students apply online or by phone at 1-888-892-2228. Conestoga's Accessible Learning and Library & Learning Services are separate ResourceHub listings.

entries.name: Community Integration through Co-operative Education (CICE) (St. Lawrence College)
entries.description: A two-year, in-person Ontario College Certificate program for adults with significant learning challenges at St. Lawrence College's Brockville campus (also offered in Kingston and Cornwall). Students follow an individualized program of study with elective courses from other programs, supported by Learning Specialists who attend classes with them, and complete field placements arranged by program staff.
entries.cost_note: Estimated fees: $2,775.78 tuition plus $987.49 ancillary fees ($3,763.27 for two semesters); students on OSAP can apply for the Bursary for Students with Disabilities.
entries.evidence: The Community Integration through Co-operative Education (CICE) program is a 2-year academic certificate program designed for adults with significant learning challenges who wish to further their education/vocational training in a community college setting.
entries.notes: CNAF's old Brockville link redirects to this page. Next start September 2027 (program code 0790); the same program runs at the Kingston (613.544.5400) and Cornwall (613.933.6080) campuses. Admission needs an OSSC/OSSD, Certificate of Accomplishment or mature status, two confidential references, and an in-person interview and skills assessment. St. Lawrence's accessibility and academic support services are separate ResourceHub listings.

entries.name: Ontario Student Assistance Program (OSAP)
entries.description: Ontario's financial aid program for postsecondary students, offering grants and loans to help eligible students pay for college, university and approved micro-credential programs. Students with a permanent or prolonged disability can get full-time OSAP while taking 40% or more of a full course load, and the same application considers them for extra aid for disability-related services and equipment.
entries.cost_note: Government grants and loans; loans must be repaid. The site does not mention an application fee.
entries.evidence: If you have a permanent disability or a persistent or prolonged disability, you could be eligible for full-time OSAP funding if you’re taking 40% or more of a full course load.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old OSAP portal (osap.gov.on.ca/OSAPPortal/index.htm), which now redirects to ontario.ca; applications are online through an OSAP account. Students are told to contact their school's financial aid office with questions; no central phone on the page. The Bursary for Students with Disabilities and the Canada Student Grant for Services and Equipment are already separate ResourceHub listings.

entries.name: Community Legal Education Ontario (CLEO)
entries.description: An Ontario organization that writes clear, practical legal information to help people understand and use their legal rights, focusing on people who face barriers such as income, disability, literacy and language. It runs the Steps to Justice website, Guided Pathways that help people fill out legal forms, and a collection of free publications in many languages; it gives general information, not legal advice.
entries.cost_note: The site describes its legal information as free, and publications can be ordered for free.
entries.evidence: Our work focuses on providing information to people who face barriers to accessing the justice system, including income, disability, literacy, and language.
entries.notes: CNAF links to a CLEO publication on getting children without immigration status into school (http://www.cleo.on.ca/en/publications/rightschool); that page is 404 and the title is not in CLEO's current resources list, so this entry is for CLEO itself. No phone or email on the pages fetched. A single Steps to Justice page is already in ResourceHub (named.json), but not CLEO as an organization.

entries.name: Ontario Special Education Tribunal (OSET)
entries.description: An independent tribunal, part of Tribunals Ontario, where parents, guardians or adult students can appeal a school board's identification or placement decision for a student with exceptional learning needs, after going through the IPRC and the Special Education Appeal Board. It offers voluntary mediation by video and hearings in English or French, can provide interpreters including sign language, and its decisions are final and binding.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention a filing fee.
entries.evidence: Learn about the Ontario Special Education Tribunal (OSET) process for appealing the identification or placement of your child with exceptional learning needs within the English or French Public or Catholic school boards.
entries.notes: CNAF links to oset-tedo.ca/eng/, which now redirects to a 404 on tribunalsontario.ca; the tribunal's current page is tribunalsontario.ca/oset/. Appeals must be filed within 30 days of the school board's decision on the SEAB recommendations (Form A: Notice of Appeal); hearings usually happen about 3 months after filing. Contact details from the OSET contact page: office at 15 Grosvenor Street, Ground Floor, Toronto; TTY through Bell Relay 1-800-855-0511.

entries.name: Hamilton Autism Services (Woodview Mental Health and Autism Services)
entries.description: Woodview's autism services in Hamilton for children, youth and adults. Programs include PEERS® social skills groups for teens and adults, a Transition to High School program, an after-school social skills respite group, the L.I.F.E. adult day program, one-to-one support, social and recreation groups, and two mid- to long-term residential programs.
