entries.evidence: Hamilton Autism Services offer supportive services to children, youth, and adults with autism to help them achieve positive outcomes as well as increased quality of life and independence.
entries.notes: CNAF calls it Woodview Children's Centre (Hamilton programs) and links to woodview.ca and an old autism-programs page that now redirects to /autism-services/; the Hamilton programs are at /hamilton-autism-services/. Woodview also runs autism services in Halton (Burlington) and Brant with their own intake contacts (see woodview.ca/autism-services/). Head office: 69 Flatt Road, Burlington. PEERS® for Teens is virtual; the young adult social group meets in person.

entries.name: Woodview Learning Centre (Woodview Mental Health and Autism Services)
entries.description: An alternative school in Burlington for children and youth with an autism diagnosis, run by Woodview Mental Health and Autism Services. Students work through a modified Ontario curriculum in small groups with an Individual Education Plan, taught by ABA instructors under an OCT-certified teacher, and families can use Ontario Autism Program funding for its ABA services.
entries.cost_note: Fee for service: tuition depends on the teaching ratio, with a non-refundable registration fee; OAP funding can be used for its ABA services.
entries.evidence: An alternative school placement of children / youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder, our interesting and effective curriculum offers a wide range of opportunities for learning these skills.
entries.notes: CNAF links to woodview.ca; the school now has its own site, woodviewlearningcentre.ca, which Woodview's autism services page links to. Key dates shown are for 2025/2026 and the footer says © 2018, so a reviewer may want to confirm 2026/2027 enrolment. Accepts families from across Southern Ontario; intake is through Woodview's Halton Autism Services Intake Coordinator (email used here).

entries.name: Manor Residential Program (Woodview Mental Health and Autism Services)
entries.description: Woodview Manor is a mid- to long-term group home in a Hamilton townhouse for up to 5 adults with autism and low support needs, with staff support for life skills goals and group social and recreational activities. Residents must live in Hamilton and qualify through Developmental Services Ontario (DSO); referrals go through Hamilton-Niagara DSO.
entries.cost_note: Living and support fees are discussed with families at an initial meeting; government funding and a partnership with Kiwanis Homes keep costs affordable.
entries.evidence: In Woodview Manor we have created a group living environment and provide supports for up to 5 individuals with Autism.
entries.notes: CNAF's Woodview Manor link (woodview.ca/autism-services/autism-programs.html) is 404; the program is now at /hamilton-autism-services/manor-residential-program/ and is listed under Woodview's Hamilton programs for adults. The phone is Hamilton-Niagara DSO's, for questions, referrals and waitlist position; openings are rare. Woodview also runs a separate Supported Independent Living program on the Hamilton Mountain with the same DSO referral route.

entries.name: Adult Clinical Services (Bethesda Services)
entries.description: Assessments, treatment, consultation and training for adults with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities in the Hamilton, Niagara, Brant, Haldimand and Norfolk regions. The team includes psychometrists, occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, social workers and behaviour consultants, offering counselling and therapy groups, caregiver support groups, speech-language services and behaviour support.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost; most services are accessed through Developmental Services Ontario (DSO).
entries.evidence: In Hamilton, Niagara, Brant, Haldimand and Norfolk Regions, Bethesda’s Adult Clinical Services provides comprehensive person-centred assessments, treatments, consults, and educational and training opportunities.
entries.notes: CNAF links to an old Twin Lakes Clinical Services page on bethesdaservices.com (404); Bethesda's adult clinical services are now at /en/adult/clinical-services. Services are accessed through DSO (occupational therapy by internal referral); psychology can assess for a developmental or intellectual disability. The page no longer lists psychiatry, which CNAF mentions. Contact details from the page footer (Thorold head office).

entries.name: Child Development Program (Holland Bloorview Kids Rehabilitation Hospital)
entries.description: An outpatient program at Holland Bloorview Kids Rehabilitation Hospital in Toronto for children and youth with diagnoses such as cerebral palsy, spina bifida, Duchenne muscular dystrophy, cleft lip and palate, autism and complex medical conditions. It offers team, clinic and individual assessment, consultation and intervention, plus specialty clinics such as feeding, complex epilepsy, neuromuscular and psychopharmacology; virtual appointments can be arranged.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: The child development program provides outpatient services to children with diagnoses such as cerebral palsy, spina bifida, Duchenne’s muscular dystrophy, cleft lip and palate, along with autism and complex medical conditions and syndromes.
entries.notes: CNAF's link (programsandservices/ProgramsServicesAZ/Childdevelopmentprogram) is 404; the program is now at /services/programs-services/child-development-program. This is separate from Holland Bloorview's Autism Diagnostic Services, which is already in ResourceHub. The page does not explain referrals; phone is the hospital's main line from the footer (toll free 800 363 2440).

entries.name: Autism Services (ErinoakKids)
entries.description: ErinoakKids' services for children with autism and their families, with sites in Brampton, Mississauga, Oakville and Orangeville. They include autism diagnostic assessment, Ontario Autism Program services (Caregiver-Mediated Early Years, Entry to School and Urgent Response Services), Applied Behaviour Analysis for children up to nine years old, respite options and free foundational services.
entries.cost_note: Foundational services are free and some programs are funded through the OAP; the page does not give other costs.
entries.evidence: ErinoakKids offers services and support to children with autism and their families, delivered by qualified, caring professionals.
entries.notes: CNAF links to erinoakkids.ca/autism-services, which now lands on ErinoakKids' 404 page; the autism services page is now at /all-services/services/autism-services. Referrals go through ErinoakKids Intake Services (phone from the Contact Us page; toll free 1-877-374-6625). ErinoakKids itself, its preschool speech program and Sibshops are already separate ResourceHub listings; this one is for its autism services.

entries.name: The Redpath Centre
entries.description: A Toronto clinic offering psychological and diagnostic assessments for children, teens and adults, covering autism, ADHD, learning disabilities, FASD, intellectual and developmental disabilities and social-emotional difficulties, with therapy, counselling and coaching after assessment. A formal diagnosis is not needed to receive its services, and people can self-refer.
entries.cost_note: Assessments are not covered by OHIP; many private insurance plans cover all or part of the cost, and students on OSAP may qualify for a bursary.
entries.evidence: We provide psychological assessments for people of all ages and in all stages of life.
entries.notes: CNAF links to /psychological-and-diagnostic-assessments/, which redirects to /assessments/. CNAF names two psychologists; the centre now lists a larger team of psychologists, therapists and coaches. Contact details from the page footer; no email address shown (contact form only).

entries.name: Bartimaeus (Ontario)
entries.description: A Canadian-owned company, founded in 1988, that gives one-to-one support to children, adolescents and adults with behavioural, mental health or developmental challenges, in the family home, hospital, school, workplace or community. Its Ontario family services include behaviour programming, in-home respite and short-term Parent Help coaching (including on autism and neurodiversity), arranged through service coordinators across Ontario.
entries.cost_note: The site does not list fees.
entries.evidence: Today Bartimaeus offers many direct services to clients with complex needs, as well as customized training and consultation services to customers throughout Ontario, Quebec and the Maritimes.
entries.notes: Ontario-based: Burlington administrative office (1006 Plains Road East) and services offices in Toronto and Barrie; Family Services coordinators cover most Ontario regions (Coordinators page). The family support page says there are no waiting lists. Bartimaeus's Quebec and Nova Scotia services are separate ResourceHub listings; this entry is for its Ontario services.

entries.name: Dr. Sala & Associates
entries.description: A psychology practice in Waterdown, in the Hamilton area, offering assessments and therapy for children, teens, adults and families in English and French. Assessments include autism, ADHD, FASD, psycho-educational, OAP-related and DSO eligibility assessments, and it runs therapy and skills groups such as an ADHD parenting group.
entries.cost_note: Fee-based (groups cost $400 to $800); it direct-bills GreenShield and Sun Life, and offers a free 15-minute consultation.
entries.evidence: We offer comprehensive autism assessments for children, youth, and adults who are seeking clarity about whether they may be on the autism spectrum.
entries.notes: CNAF links to drsala.com, which redirects to drsala.ca; CNAF calls it Dr. Michelle Sala & Associates, and the site uses Dr. Sala & Associates. Contact details from the home page (Mon to Fri, 9am to 5pm); the free consultation is virtual and groups are in person.

entries.name: Family Kinnections
entries.description: A psychotherapy practice offering counselling and therapy for children, teens, parents and families, in person in Welland or by secure video across Ontario. It describes itself as neurodiversity-affirming and trauma-informed, supports concerns such as ADHD, autistic children and teens, anxiety, school distress and challenging behaviour, and runs groups for parents, kids and teens.
entries.cost_note: Fee-based; may be covered by extended health plans, NIHB or Ontario Autism Program funding. The first consultation is free and the site says there are no wait-lists.
entries.evidence: Counselling and psychotherapy for children, teens, parents, and families — grounded in safety, connection, and real respect for your family's needs.
entries.notes: CNAF lists Meghan Lederman, Registered Psychotherapist, with offices in Hamilton, Oakville and Welland; the site now shows one office in Welland plus online sessions, and its clinical director is Meghan Maynard (the practice is a division of Meghan Maynard Psychotherapy Professional Corporation), so CNAF's details may be out of date. Another Ontario sheet also links familykinnections.ca, so check for a duplicate.

entries.name: Hope Autism Services
entries.description: Hope Autism Services is an autism therapy centre in Mississauga, founded in 2009 by Kay Narula, that provides Ontario Autism Program (OAP) eligible services. It offers ABA therapy, speech-language pathology, occupational therapy, psychological supports, autism diagnosis and assessments, weekend ABA and camps for children and youth, in centre, at home, in schools and the community, or online.
entries.cost_note: Private fees; the centre's own rates are not listed. Its funding page says ABA therapy in Ontario can cost $50 to $200 per hour and that OAP funding or private insurance may cover costs. The first consultation is free.
entries.address: 150 Britannia Rd E, #8, Mississauga ON, L4Z 2A4
entries.evidence: Hope Autism Services is an OAP-approved autism centre in Mississauga, offering ABA, SLP, OT, psychological and in-home therapy
entries.notes: CNAF links to a Psychology Today profile of founder Kay Narula, which now redirects to Psychology Today's generic US search page. The practice's own site is hopeautism.ca (hopeautismservices.com redirects there). Contact details from the home and contact pages; the site title also mentions Vaughan, but only the Mississauga clinic address is listed. Ages from the about page ("from early learners to teens").

entries.name: Adult Neurodevelopmental Services (Centre for Addiction and Mental Health)
entries.description: An outpatient program at CAMH in Toronto for people 16 and older with an intellectual disability and/or autism who have mental health concerns or behaviours that challenge, offering short-term assessment and treatment from psychiatrists, psychologists, behaviour therapists, occupational therapists, social workers and a nurse. It also offers autism diagnostic assessments for adults 18 and older; autism assessment and psychiatry serve all of Ontario.
entries.cost_note: The page does not list fees; it calls its autism assessments publicly funded. A physician or nurse practitioner referral is required.
entries.evidence: This service provides short-term, inter-professional goal-oriented assessment and treatment to adults diagnosed with intellectual disabilities or autism. ANS also offers autism diagnostic assessments.
entries.notes: CNAF links to CAMH's old home page (now camh.ca) and describes a former children's Pervasive Developmental Disorders service; CAMH's current autism service is Adult Neurodevelopmental Services (CNAF also names it under item 200). Outpatient mental health services need a confirmed diagnosis of intellectual disability and/or autism; the wait for autism assessment is "several years long" and some groups are paused. Other disciplines serve Toronto (M postal codes) only.

entries.name: Bridging to Adulthood (Holland Bloorview Kids Rehabilitation Hospital)
entries.description: A Holland Bloorview team (a social worker, a life skills facilitator and a pro bono lawyer) that helps youth with disabilities aged 14 to 18, up to 21 if still in high school, and their families plan for adult life before pediatric care ends at 18. It offers personal consultations (virtual, by phone or in person), a monthly virtual welcome session, and pop-up workshops on topics such as ODSP, Developmental Services Ontario, legal planning and finding adult primary care.
entries.cost_note: Holland Bloorview's program guide lists the fees for Bridging to Adulthood as "none".
entries.address: 150 Kilgour Road, Toronto Ontario Canada M4G 1R8
entries.evidence: Holland Bloorview’s Bridging to Adulthood Team supports youth with disabilities – and their families – who need help planning meaningful goals for adulthood when pediatric care ends at age 18.
entries.notes: CNAF links to Holland Bloorview's Door to Adulthood page (hollandbloorview.ca/door2adulthood/default.htm), which is now 404. Holland Bloorview's current transition-to-adulthood service is Bridging to Adulthood, part of its Transitions, Recreation and Life Skills program; a reviewer may want to confirm it is the successor. Open to current or former clients and to self-referrals from the community. ResourceHub already lists other Holland Bloorview services (SibKits, sibling support, autism diagnostic services, nursery school), not this one.

entries.name: Ontario Health atHome
entries.description: Ontario's provincial agency that coordinates home and community care, long-term care placement and referrals to community services. Care coordinators assess needs and arrange services such as nursing and personal support at home, and its School Health Support Services help students with complex health needs or disabilities attend school. Anyone, including the person themselves, can make a referral by phone.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: We are Ontario Health atHome, a single organization coordinating local home and community care, long-term care placement and help finding services in the community.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old health.gov.on.ca list of Community Care Access Centres (CCACs), which no longer resolves. Home and community care coordination once done by the CCACs is now done by Ontario Health atHome (14 local offices; a postal-code office finder is on the site). The site itself does not mention CCACs, so a reviewer may want to confirm the match. For school health supports in the Champlain area the site points families to CHEO.

entries.name: Autism Spectrum Disorder Services (Niagara Children's Centre)
entries.description: Niagara Children's Centre in St. Catharines supports children and youth diagnosed with autism and their families with assessment, early intervention, diagnosis, occupational therapy, physiotherapy, speech-language pathology, social work, preschool resource consulting, school-based rehabilitation and recreational therapy. With its partners it provides autism diagnostic assessments for Niagara children aged 0 to 4 and the OAP caregiver-mediated early years and entry to school programs.
entries.cost_note: The page says the OAP caregiver-mediated early years program is free of charge; it does not state costs for its other autism services.
entries.address: 567 Glenridge Avenue St. Catharines, ON L2T 4C2
entries.evidence: Niagara Children’s Centre supports children and youth diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder, as well as their families, with a variety of programs and services.
entries.notes: CNAF links to npcc.on.ca (Niagara Peninsula Children's Centre), which now redirects to niagarachildrenscentre.com. ResourceHub already lists the centre's Early Years (0-4) services; this entry is its autism services page, a different program. Diagnostic services are for Niagara residents aged 0 to 4 with a physician referral; the OAP programs are by invitation and registered through Bethesda (905-684-6918 ext. 170).

entries.name: Red Roof Retreat
entries.description: A charity in Niagara-on-the-Lake that provides respite and recreation programs for children, youth and young adults with special needs and their families in the Niagara Region. Programs include weekend respite on its farm, a day program, Saturday camp, youth nights and summer camps.
entries.cost_note: Weekend respite costs $200 for children and $275 for adults per weekend (subject to change); receipts can be submitted to Special Services at Home for reimbursement.
entries.address: 1594 Concession 6 Rd, Niagara-on-the-Lake, ON L0S 1J0, Canada
entries.evidence: Here at Red Roof Retreat, we provide quality respite and recreational programs to children, youth and young adults with special needs and their families in the Niagara Region
entries.notes: Weekend respite is for ages 3 to 18, and for adults 19+ only if previously enrolled; there is a waiting list for respite. It cannot offer one-to-one support (it is not government funded). Contact details from the contact page.

entries.name: Children at Risk
entries.description: An Ottawa charity that supports families in the Greater Ottawa area whose children are diagnosed with autism. It runs Camp Kaleidoscope (a summer day camp), a March Break camp and Saturday Fun Club activity and respite sessions for children and youth aged 4 to 18+, and works on autism awareness and advocacy.
entries.cost_note: Summer camp is $900 per week in 2026 (the charity says its own cost is over $2,900 per camper per week, with donors covering the difference); Saturday Fun Club is $125 per session; a $75 yearly membership is required.
entries.address: 1590 Liverpool Court, Unit 8, Ottawa ON K1B 4L2
entries.evidence: At Children at Risk, we are dedicated to supporting families in the Greater Ottawa area with children diagnosed within the autism spectrum disorders.
entries.notes: CNAF links to a 2005 PDF directory on childrenatrisk.ca (now HTTP 400); this entry is the charity that published it. 2026 summer camp registration is closed with a full waitlist, and Fall/Winter Saturday Fun Club dates are "to be announced". A membership is required for its programs.

entries.name: Special Olympics Ontario
entries.description: A charity that offers year-round sport training and competition for people with an intellectual disability, cognitive delay or developmental disability, including autism, in more than 100 communities across Ontario. Programs include community sports, Unified Champion Schools, Active Start and FUNdamentals play programs for young children, health programs, and provincial, national and world games.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.address: 65 Overlea Boulevard, Suite 200 Toronto, Ontario M4H 1P1
entries.evidence: Special Olympics Ontario is dedicated to enriching the lives of Ontarians with an intellectual disability through sport.
entries.notes: CNAF links to an old page (specialolympicsontario.com/default.asp?contentID=189, now 404); the site now redirects to www1.specialolympicsontario.com. Eligibility: intellectual disability, cognitive delay or developmental disability (autism is listed); athletes can start at age 2. Athlete registration is online through portal.specialolympics.ca. Address and phone are the provincial office's, from the Our Team page.

entries.name: Transitions, Recreation and Life Skills (Holland Bloorview Kids Rehabilitation Hospital)
entries.description: An interdisciplinary team at Holland Bloorview (therapeutic recreation specialists, life skills coaches, social workers and an occupational therapist) that runs community-integrated programs for children, youth and young adults with disabilities, most for ages 7 to 18 (up to 21 if in high school). Programs include life skills coaching and groups, adapted sports and recreation, an adapted equipment loan program, virtual friendship groups, employment participation, post-secondary transition support, and The Independence Program, a 3-week overnight life skills program for ages 17 to 21.
entries.cost_note: Fees vary by program: life skills programs have program-specific fees and some recreation activities have fees, while the equipment loan, Friendship & Belonging, employment, post-secondary and Bridging to Adulthood programs are listed as free or with no fees.
entries.address: 150 Kilgour Road, Toronto Ontario Canada M4G 1R8
entries.evidence: Our team works closely with community partners to support personal goals, social connections, and skill development though experiential learning opportunities. Most programs are designed for clients ages 7 – 18yrs (up to 21 if in high school).
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old "Therapeutic recreation and life skills" page (hollandbloorview.ca/programsandservices/Therapeuticrecreationandlifeskills), now 404; the program is now Transitions, Recreation and Life Skills. Most programs are for Holland Bloorview clients (several accept self-referral); waitlists range from none to about a year depending on the program (life skills 6 to 9 months). ResourceHub already lists other Holland Bloorview services, not this one; Bridging to Adulthood (item 179) is a separate entry.

entries.name: Music Therapy Association of Ontario (MTAO)
entries.description: The professional association for music therapists in Ontario. Its Find a Therapist directory lets people search for Accredited Music Therapists by area, client age group and population served (autism is one option), and its referral form sends a request to members, who contact the person if they can provide the service.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: The following directory provides several ways to locate an Accredited Music Therapist. You may filter them below by geographical area, age group or client populations.
entries.notes: CNAF links to /find-a-music-therapist (now 404); the directory is now at /find-a-therapist/. The home page currently shows WordPress placeholder privacy-policy text, but the directory, about and contact pages are current. Email from the contact page; age groups from the directory filters (infants to older adults).

entries.name: Autism Services (Speech Therapy Centres of Canada)
entries.description: A private speech-language pathology clinic with offices in Markham and Ajax and virtual care across Ontario. Its speech-language pathologists provide individualized assessment and therapy for autistic children and youth, including those who use few words, communicate through scripts or echolalia, or find conversation difficult.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed; the site says OAP funding may apply to eligible speech-language pathology services.
entries.address: 8300 Woodbine Avenue, Suite 200 Markham, ON L3R 9Y7
entries.evidence: Speech Therapy Centres of Canada provides individualized Autism Services in Toronto and the GTA for children and youth with communication needs involving language, social communication, speech clarity, conversation, play and everyday participation.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old /areas/autismspectrum/ page (now 404); the autism page is now /autism-spectrum-disorder-asd/. Head office and main clinic in Markham, kids clinic in Ajax (300 Rossland Rd. E., Suite 301); virtual care across Ontario. The page notes that a speech-language assessment does not replace an autism diagnostic assessment.

entries.name: The Speech Associates
entries.description: A speech-language pathology and ABA provider whose clinicians see children and adults at home or online across Ontario. Services include speech and language therapy led by CASLPO-registered speech-language pathologists, ABA and behavioural therapies led by registered behaviour analysts, social communication support and adult autism therapy.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed; registration has no enrolment fee, and the site has a page on Ontario Autism Program (OAP) funding.
entries.evidence: Our dedicated network of Speech and Behaviour Specialists across Ontario are ready to provide you service in your home, online, or a combination of both.
entries.notes: CNAF links to /index.php (now 404); the home page is speechassociates.ca. It lists service locations in Toronto, Etobicoke, North York, Scarborough, Pickering/Ajax, Oshawa and other areas (main Toronto location 31 Prince Arthur Ave); therapy is mostly in the home or online. Its intake line is open 7 days a week.

entries.name: Dr Erin Warriner, Clinical Psychologists & Neuropsychologists
entries.description: A private clinical psychology and neuropsychology practice in Hamilton serving Hamilton, Halton, Brant, Niagara and nearby areas. It offers developmental and school-entry assessments for young children, psychoeducational and diagnostic assessments, neuropsychological assessments, cognitive rehabilitation and psychotherapy for children, adults and seniors; autism spectrum disorders are among the concerns it assesses.
entries.cost_note: Private fee-for-service (not covered by OHIP), based on Ontario Psychological Association fee guidelines; payment by cash, cheque or money order at the time of service; may be covered by extended health or auto insurance.
entries.address: 1100 South Service Road, Suite 224 Hamilton, ON L8E 0C5
entries.evidence: Dr Warriner opened her own private practice in 2009, providing developmental, psychological, psychoeducational, and neuropsychological diagnostic assessments and treatment to children, adults and seniors.
entries.notes: Contact details from the home and contact pages; bookings are by email to Dr. Warriner's own address (left out here) or by phone. Office in the Hamilton Business Park. The site shows character-encoding errors, but an associate's 2022 training is listed, so it has been updated recently.

entries.name: Developmental Dual Diagnosis Program (St. Joseph's Healthcare Hamilton)
entries.description: A hospital outpatient program in Hamilton that provides community-based mental health care for adults 18 and older with intellectual and developmental disabilities, including autism, who have mental health concerns. Its team of psychiatrists, nurses, an occupational therapist and social workers offers assessment, treatment recommendations and medication, and education and support for clients, families and caregivers.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost; patients are asked to bring their Ontario health card (OHIP).
entries.address: 100 West 5th Street Level 2, Block B, Room B228 Hamilton ON L8N 3K7
entries.evidence: We provide community-based mental health services, to help adults with developmental disabilities and mental health concerns.
entries.notes: ResourceHub already lists St. Joseph's Youth Wellness Centre on the same site; this is a different program. It serves people living in Hamilton-Wentworth, Niagara, Brant, Burlington and Haldimand-Norfolk (others can call to ask). Referrals go through St. Joe's Connect central intake, and a family doctor or psychiatrist must be involved. CNAF says 17+; the page now says 18 and older.

entries.name: Bayridge Counselling Centres, Hamilton office
entries.description: The Hamilton office of Bayridge Counselling Centres, a private counselling practice. Its therapists offer counselling for adults, couples, families, children and teens, in person or online, and intake specialists match each client with a therapist.
entries.cost_note: Sessions start at $90 and vary by therapist; often covered by benefit plans.
entries.address: 565 Sanatorium Rd., Unit 203, Hamilton, ON L9C 7N4
entries.evidence: Warm, evidence-based counselling in Hamilton — in person or securely online. Reach out and we'll match you with a therapist who fits.
entries.notes: Bayridge's site also lists autism (ASD) assessments for adults and for children and youth across its offices. The Hamilton office is in the Sir William Osler Health Institute Building, wheelchair accessible, with free parking. Contact details from the Hamilton page.

entries.name: Family Services Perth-Huron
entries.description: A non-profit charity based in Stratford that provides counselling and developmental support services across Perth, Huron, Grey and Bruce counties. For families of children with developmental disabilities it offers Special Services at Home coordination, respite (including the Rotary Respite House in Stratford), a family support worker and a social skills group for autistic youth aged 11 to 14; for adults with developmental disabilities it offers protective service workers, life skills programs and the Familyhome home-sharing program.
entries.cost_note: The first counselling appointment is free; whether fees apply depends on the program, and some programs are fully subsidized.
entries.address: 142 Waterloo St. South Stratford, ON N5A 4B4
entries.evidence: Supports are available for children and adults with developmental disabilities to become more involved in their communities.
entries.notes: Offices also in Clinton, Listowel and Owen Sound. Adult developmental services need eligibility from Developmental Services Ontario; the social skills group is for youth with level 1 autism. Contact details from the home page; no general email is listed.

entries.name: One-to-One Program (C.Y.O. Camp Marydale)
entries.description: Camp Marydale, the Catholic Youth Organization's day camp at Marydale Park near Hamilton, includes children with special needs aged 4 to 12 in its regular camp programs with a trained one-to-one counsellor. Support is offered for PA days, Christmas Break, March Break and summer camp, and covers help with walking, eating, hygiene, social interactions and medications.
entries.cost_note: There is no extra fee for one-to-one support: families pay the same as other campers (a $275.00 registration fee), with fundraising and camp subsidies covering the rest.
entries.address: 5999 Chippewa Road East Mount Hope Ontario L0R 1W0
entries.evidence: Please note that we are now happy to accept special needs campers ages 4-12 years old, providing them with one-to-one support during all our programs: PA day, Christmas Break, March Break and Summer Camp!
entries.notes: CNAF links to cyo.on.ca/campmarydale/about-us/ (now 404); Camp Marydale now has its own site, campmarydale.ca. For families in Hamilton-Wentworth and surrounding communities; only one week per child is guaranteed, with a waiting list for more. The C.Y.O. also offers One-to-One at its overnight Camp Brébeuf in Rockwood (cyo.on.ca/one-to-one-program). The address is the camp's mailing address; the email is the camp director's role address.

entries.name: Camp Kennebec
entries.description: An overnight summer camp near Arden, Ontario for campers aged 6 and up with learning disabilities and developmental delays, including autism, ADHD, Down syndrome, OCD, brain injury and anxiety. Sessions run 1 to 8 weeks with a 2:1 camper-to-cabin-staff ratio and more than 50 activities, plus a leaders-in-training program for teens and a life and job skills program for young adults 18+.
entries.cost_note: Summer 2027 fees run up to $15,500 plus HST for the 8-week session; the site has a page on funding sources.
entries.evidence: summer camp for campers with learning disabilities, and developmental delays including autism, Asperger’s, ADHD, Down Syndrome, OCD, brain injury, anxiety, social skill and other challenges
entries.notes: Accredited by the Ontario Camps Association and the Canadian Camping Association (per its site). Some weeks fill up; the office can check availability or add campers to a waitlist. Contact details from the site footer.

entries.name: Camp Kodiak
entries.description: An integrated, non-competitive overnight summer camp in McKellar, Ontario for children and teens aged 6 to 18 with and without learning disabilities, ADHD and ASD Level 1 (low support needs). It offers a 2-to-1 camper-to-staff ratio, a social skills program, small cabin groups, academic tutoring, over 50 activities and a leader-in-training program for ages 16 to 18.
entries.cost_note: 2027 rates start at $4,455.00 plus HST for a 2-week session, all inclusive.
entries.address: 200 Kodiak Road McKellar, Ontario, Canada, P0G 1C0
entries.evidence: Camp Kodiak is an overnight summer camp for kids and teens (6 to 18 years old) with and without Learning Disabilities, ADHD and ASD Level 1 (low support needs).
entries.notes: For autistic campers, only ASD Level 1 (low support needs). The address is the summer camp; the winter office is in Mississauga. Its program for adults 19+ is Club Kodiak (item 225, separate entry).

entries.name: Club Kodiak
entries.description: An overnight summer program near Burk's Falls, Ontario for neurodivergent adults aged 19 and older, including people with learning disabilities, ADHD, ASD (low support needs) and mild intellectual disability. Guests choose sports, arts and recreation activities in a resort setting, with a life skills and social skills program and a 3:1 guest-to-staff ratio.
entries.cost_note: 2027 fees run from $4,262.00 for 2 weeks to $15,925.00 for 9 weeks, plus HST and day-trip money.
entries.evidence: Club Kodiak is a unique overnight summer program for adults 19+ who are neurodivergent.
entries.notes: Guests need to manage personal care on their own, communicate with spoken words and handle stairs and uneven terrain (see the about page). Burk's Falls comes from the site's page title; no street address is listed. Its program for children aged 6 to 18 is Camp Kodiak (item 223).

entries.name: One-on-One Support at Sport Fitness School (McMaster Athletics & Recreation Camps)
entries.description: McMaster University's summer multi-sport day camp in Hamilton offers one-on-one support so children with an exceptionality can take part in the integrated camp. Trained volunteer coaches, a one-on-one coordinator and occupational therapists support campers aged 6 to 16; families complete an application and a needs assessment form.
entries.cost_note: Summer 2026 one-on-one sessions cost $370.00 per week ($315.00 for the 4-day week).
entries.evidence: Sport Fitness School strives to provide integrated sport for athletes who identify with an exceptionality. Our One-on-One Coordinator and Occupational Therapists provide tools for athletes to be successful in large and small group settings.
entries.notes: Covers two CNAF items: McMaster Camps (rec.mcmaster.ca/programs/youth-camps-march-break-summer, which redirects here) and Special Needs & One-on-One Support (rec.mcmaster.ca/programs/youth-camps/special-needs-one-one-support, now 404). One-on-one support is only at Sport Fitness School summer sessions, up to two sessions per camper; all registrations are waitlisted and reviewed, and support is not available on buses or in extended care. Phone and email are the SFS office's.

entries.name: Helping Hands 1:1 Inclusion Program (YMCA Hamilton | Burlington | Brantford)
entries.description: A YMCA day camp program that gives children aged 6 to 15 with physical and/or developmental disabilities one-to-one support from trained Helping Hands staff, so they can join regular summer day camp programming with their peers. YMCA day camps run in Hamilton, Burlington and Brantford.
entries.cost_note: The page does not list camp fees or say whether Helping Hands costs extra.
entries.evidence: Helping Hands offers 1:1 support for children with physical and/or developmental disabilities so they can enjoy a summer camp experience alongside their peers.
entries.notes: ResourceHub already lists YMCA HBB Immigrant Services and a YMCA location on the same site; this is a different program. CNAF's link (/Programs/Categories/Camps/Day-Camps) now redirects to /camp/day-camp. Day camp locations include Queen Victoria School (Hamilton), Tansley Woods Community Centre (Burlington) and Laurier Brantford YMCA.
